name: inquiry-customer-goal
change_from_v1: LABELS ONLY. The product owner adjudicated classes A, B and C on 2026-09-20; D, E and F stay open. No row was added or removed, the unit is unchanged, and v1 stays frozen and readable — it is the version the contract was designed against.

adjudications.R:4181864b n1: ACTION (was provisional no-goal) — directly implied request to expedite. NOT reinterpreted as STATE_READ merely because order-state reading is what this system can do.
adjudications.S:T10b n1: INFORMATION (referent moved CURRENT_ORDER -> CURRENT_LISTING) — first establish whether the delivered quantity matches the listing. No remedy is inferred before that fact is observed.
adjudications.R:8989a9d0 n1: INFORMATION — pre-purchase availability question. Missing knowledge may later require seller input; that does not turn the customer's requested outcome into DECISION.
adjudications.S:T12a n1: DECISION — asks whether the existing order's address CAN be changed; does not yet request the change.
adjudications.S:N2 n1: ACTION — explicitly requests an external action. Executor availability must not alter customer-goal semantics.

no_goal_is_not_ignore: R:0c582144 emits no customer resolution goal. The case still exists and may raise VOC / complaint / issue signals elsewhere in Reviewnary; what it does not carry is a goal for this loop to resolve.
the_check: build.py no longer asserts that every outcome agrees with the frozen closing_authority — the ruling was explicit that the old gold must not be forced to remain valid. It asserts instead that every DISAGREEMENT IS DECLARED in LEGACY_CONFLICTS with a reason. A new, undeclared disagreement still fails the build, so the check stays falsifiable while recording the decision.

legacy_conflicts.what_they_are: 5 resolution-gold rows (inquiry-resolution-plan/v3.3) whose closing authority or whole step list no longer follows from the adjudicated customer goal. They are IDENTIFIED here and deliberately NOT re-derived: re-labelling the frozen resolution gold is a separate decision with its own evidence rows.
legacy_conflicts.R:0c582144 n1: GOAL_OBSOLETE — no goal is emitted, so the resolution goal has no subject.
legacy_conflicts.R:4181864b n1: CLOSER_MOVES — ENTITY_STATE -> PROCEDURE; the order read becomes a procedure prerequisite.
legacy_conflicts.S:T10b n1: PLAN_OBSOLETE — the whole step list (order read + procedure + org policy) belongs to a remedy, not to an information question.
legacy_conflicts.S:T12a n1: CLOSER_MOVES — PROCEDURE -> KNOWLEDGE/SELLER; the ENTITY.ORDER read survives as the decision rule's prerequisite.
legacy_conflicts.S:N2 n1: NO_CAPABILITY — ACTION requires a procedure this registry does not have at all. The row cannot close on any authority currently registered, and that is the honest reading.

decision_prerequisite_audit.question: does DECISION -> KNOWLEDGE -> SELLER hold, or does a decision sometimes need observed entity state first?
decision_prerequisite_audit.method: read from the FROZEN gold's recorded steps, not from an opinion: for every DECISION goal, which required capabilities are neither KNOWLEDGE nor SELLER.

rows.S:T7a n1: ENTITY.LISTING — already written in the frozen gold
rows.S:T7b n1: ENTITY.LISTING — already written in the frozen gold

decision_prerequisite_audit.finding: the fixed sequence DECISION -> KNOWLEDGE -> SELLER is insufficient, and this was TRUE BEFORE S:T12a was reclassified: two of the three rows carry the entity read in the frozen gold itself. The dispatch table is still right — knowledge is asked first because the decision RULE is knowledge and the rule declares its own prerequisites — but the loop had to be able to come back.

label_policy.author: designer packet 2026-09-20; classes A/B/C adjudicated by the product owner the same day (DEV/CALIBRATION — never a holdout)
label_policy.unit: one row per frozen resolution goal, unchanged from v1. A row may emit no goal.
label_policy.principles: 1 goals express what the customer requested, not what the system can do; 2-5 the four outcome definitions; 6 surface grammar alone does not classify a 'can you...?'; 7 resolver prerequisites are not separate customer goals; 8 capability availability does not enter the label; 9 no future follow-up work is added as a goal.

holds: real inquiry id prefixes, designer labels and constraint COUNTS; no customer or seller text
